solves.reason: (A) damage - brain-damaged context confirms. (B) necessary - regions needed for forming. (C) revealed - study disclosed separate systems.
(A) intact - visual areas OK but language areas damaged. (B) difficulty - great difficulty identifying. (C) independently - do not work independently but interact.
(A) benefit from - patients do not benefit from imagery. (B) continually - are continually interacting. (C) recognition - object recognition.
④ optional is wrong; regions ARE necessary for forming visual images. Other markers contextually appropriate.
② impaired contradicts context: visual areas are OK (intact) while language areas are damaged. impaired would reverse the meaning.
① cooperatively replaces independently. Original: 'do not work independently' means they DO interact. 'do not work cooperatively' reverses meaning.
visual ___: imagery fits. 'visual imagery when trying to memorize words' matches context.
revealed ___ verbal and nonverbal systems: separate describes the relationship between the two systems.
object ___ and imagery-based memory: recognition completes the parallel phrase.
suggests ≈ indicates. Both mean 'to show/point to'. demand/deny/prevent are unrelated.
enable ≈ allow. Both mean 'make possible'. restrict/prevent are antonyms.
identifying ≈ recognizing. Both mean 'to determine what something is'.
reveal ↔ conceal. expose/uncover/display are all synonyms of reveal.
interact ↔ operate in isolation. cooperate/collaborate/communicate are all similar to interact.
(A) 'to access the second floor' = verb 접근하다. (B) 'have access to' = noun 접근. Answer: (A) 접근하다 (B) 접근.
'not damaged or changed; remaining complete and whole' = intact. separate/verbal/necessary don't match.
necessary FOR + V-ing. Preposition 'for' requires gerund: forming.
have no problems + V-ing / have difficulty + V-ing. Both require gerund: identifying.
Contrast structure: access to nonverbal system BUT problems accessing ___. The opposing system is 'verbal identity system'.
object recognition AND ___: parallel structure requires another skill noun phrase. imagery-based memory fits.
